task_metadata.research_topic: Inner learning dynamics of chunk-wise test-time memory modules (Titans / Nested Learning) — surprise signal, online update rule, data-dependent forget gate, storage structure.
task_metadata.research_question: How should a chunk-wise test-time memory module that updates its fast weights online from a surprise signal be designed — what surprise loss, update rule, and forget-gate parameterization give the best length generalization (NIAH passkey at 1.5x / 2x training context) and downstream-accuracy lift when co-trained with a fixed 345M GPT substrate?
notes: The 345M GPT (24L/16H/1024D) trained Chinchilla-optimal ~7.1B tokens on ClimbMix is the *evaluation substrate*, not the research question. The substrate is held fixed; only the memory module varies between baselines.

Length-generalization is the primary target: training context is 1024, but NIAH passkey retrieval is evaluated at 1280 / 1536 / 2048 with NTK-aware RoPE base scaling — so the only thing that can carry information past the cliff is the memory module's online consolidation.
Score spec uses niah_pass_1536, niah_pass_2k, and niah_rank_2k (continuous companion); niah_pass_1280 is recorded but excluded from scoring because it saturates near 1.0.

tests.label: gpt-345m
tests.notes: 345M pretraining on ClimbMix; reports val_loss + WikiText-2 / LAMBADA PPL.

tests.label: lm-eval-345m
tests.notes: 0-shot downstream evaluation on the 345M checkpoint (ARC-Easy, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande).

tests.label: niah-eval-345m
tests.notes: Standalone NIAH passkey retrieval at 1280 / 1536 / 2048 with NTK-aware RoPE base scaling; reports pass@1 and mean rank per length.

baselines.name: titans_default
baselines.notes: Titans Eq. 13-14 reference: depth=2 MLP memory, MSE surprise, momentum SGD with all three data-dependent gates (alpha_t/eta_t/theta_t = sigmoid(W·x)) per Titans §3.2 chunk-wise simplification.

baselines.name: linear_memory
baselines.notes: Titans §3.1 / Table 5 depth ablation: L_M = 1 (linear regression memory), otherwise identical to titans_default — clean depth ablation.

baselines.name: deep_momentum
baselines.notes: Nested Learning DMGD (§4 Eq. 51): m_{i+1} = alpha_{i+1} m_i − eta_t · phi(grad), W_{i+1} = W_i + m_{i+1}. NO weight decay on W; learnable feature map phi (small SiLU MLP) on the gradient. Depth=2 MLP memory.

baselines.name: fast_weights_hebbian
baselines.notes: Ba et al. 2016 NeurIPS Eq. 1+5: A(t) = lambda·A(t-1) + eta·h h^T autoassociative outer product, lambda=0.95, eta=0.5; inner-loop read with LayerNorm (S=1 step). NO surprise gradient — pure Hebbian storage.

papers.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
papers.relevance: Defines the Titans NMM (deep MLP memory + momentum + data-dependent forget gate) and the depth=1 vs depth>=2 ablation that motivates linear_memory.

papers.title: Nested Learning: The Illusion of Deep Learning Architecture
papers.relevance: Introduces Deep Momentum Gradient Descent (DMGD, §4 Eq. 51) — momentum with learnable feature map on the gradient. Source for deep_momentum baseline.

papers.title: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
papers.relevance: Hebbian outer-product fast-weight memory with iterative LN-stabilized inner-loop read. Source for fast_weights_hebbian baseline.
